prompt: The platform lead wants us to stop debating how RelayRoom releases reach production. Review the material in this folder and write a decision record at decisions/0007-deploy-strategy.md. Choose exactly one of rolling, blue/green, or canary, explain why the other two do not fit, and turn the operational limits into practical rollout and rollback rules. End the document with its last fenced ```json block containing one object. The object must have decision (string, one option name), options (list of objects with name and verdict strings, where verdict is chosen or rejected, plus reasons as a list of strings), constraints (list of objects with id, text, and source strings, where source is the path of the file in this folder the constraint came from), and revisitWhen (list of strings). Include units for counts, percentages, minutes, dollars, hosts, and sessions. Times must be ISO 8601 UTC. Keep the record specific enough for the on-call team to use.

rubric.criterion: The prose gives an on-call engineer a clear, service-specific explanation of the trade-offs and the chosen rollout behavior (code cannot check this because the automated key only inspects structured values and selected evidence patterns).

Score the share of expertKey items the document addresses; an item counts only when the judge quotes the passage that addresses it, and the weak answers earn nothing. Do not reward length or formatting. (code cannot check this because the items are engineering judgment, not a pattern in the text)

items.text: Sizes the first stage by how many users a bad release may reach before it is detected, and ties that size to the detection signal and its delay.
items.source: Martin Fowler, BlueGreenDeployment, https://martinfowler.com/bliki/BlueGreenDeployment.html (copyright Martin Fowler; idea only)

items.text: Handles long-lived sessions: how connections drain or move during each option, and what users see.
items.source: Google SRE book, Release Engineering, https://sre.google/sre-book/release-engineering/ (CC BY-NC-ND 4.0; idea only)

items.text: Sequences schema changes across the period when two versions run (add first, remove only after the old version is gone), not only notes that both must work.
items.source: Martin Fowler, ParallelChange, https://martinfowler.com/bliki/ParallelChange.html (copyright Martin Fowler; idea only)

items.text: Explains how a rollback treats sessions already on the new version, and how that fits the revert limit given the drain time.
items.source: Google SRE workbook, Canarying Releases, https://sre.google/workbook/canarying-releases/ (CC BY-NC-ND 4.0; idea only)

items.text: If canary is considered, says what traffic share and metrics make the canary signal meaningful for this service.
items.source: Google SRE workbook, Canarying Releases, https://sre.google/workbook/canarying-releases/ (CC BY-NC-ND 4.0; idea only)

items.text: Names the signals that decide go or stop at each stage and how long to watch them before widening.
items.source: Google SRE workbook, Canarying Releases, https://sre.google/workbook/canarying-releases/ (CC BY-NC-ND 4.0; idea only)

weakAnswers: Blue/green is best practice and gives zero downtime.
Canary, because large companies use it.
Rolling update, because it is the platform default.
A pros and cons table with no tie to the service's numbers.

All key identifiers (40-host fleet, 72% utilization, 12-minute revert window, 40-minute drain, 4 host canary, 342 line log citation) are explicitly stated in the fixture. The request defines the decision options, output format, and constraint source requirements precisely.
